subject.title: fix(memory): exclude extraPaths from shared scope hash to avoid unnecessary reindexing

question: Should same-workspace memory-source agents share one SQLite store by default when session indexing can be enabled, and what migration/API contract must accompany that change?
rationale: The PR changes persistent storage identity and possible session visibility boundaries, so automation cannot safely decide whether the product boundary should be directory-level sharing, agent-scoped storage, or an opt-in shared-store model.

options.title: Redesign before merge
options.body: Keep this PR open but require an accepted storage/session contract, doctor migration or explicit rebuild warning, and latest-head proof before changing the default DB path.

options.title: Accept directory-level sharing
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly approve same-workspace sharing as the boundary, but the PR should then document and test the migration, session visibility, and SDK lifecycle consequences.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: If the boundary is not ready, leave the canonical issue as the design thread and close or replace this implementation later with a narrower approved path.

recommendation.title: Redesign before merge
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but require an accepted storage/session contract, doctor migration or explicit rebuild warning, and latest-head proof before changing the default DB path.

likelyOwner.reason: The question spans memory resolver ownership, plugin SDK exports, and storage boundary policy; this person has the strongest recent cross-surface history in the affected files.
